# Technico Pty Limited (Australia) — FY25 Turnover

## What the report saysTechnico Pty Limited, Australia registered a turnover of Australian Dollars (A$) 2.86 million (previous year A$ 1.69 million) and a Net Profit of A$ 1.51 million (previous year A$ 0.81 million) [ITC-FY25#0377, p.98]. That is a rise of roughly 69% on the prior year's turnover, with net profit close to doubling.

Technico Pty Limited is a 100%-owned Australian subsidiary of ITC [ITC-FY25#1218, p.299], and it focuses on upgradation and commercialisation of its TECHNITUBER® Seed Technology, and is also engaged in marketing TECHNITUBER® seed produced at the facilities of its subsidiary in China and Technico Agri Sciences Limited, India, to global customers [ITC-FY25#0376, p.97].

## In Indian rupees

**At today's rate (~₹67.29 per A$1, mid-market rate quoted by currencyrate.today, 28 September 2026):**

A$ 2.86 million × 67.2859 = **₹192.4 million, i.e. about ₹19.24 crore**

**For comparison, at the rate ITC itself used:** the company's subsidiary statement (Form AOC-1) applies an exchange rate on the last day of the financial year of 53.8100 for the Australian Dollar, and reports Technico Pty Limited's turnover as 20.43 (₹ crore) [ITC-FY25#1016, p.246]. A$2.86m × 53.81 gives ₹153.9 million (₹15.39 crore) — the small gap versus ITC's ₹20.43 crore arises because ITC converts turnover at an average rate for the year rather than the closing rate, and because A$2.86m is a rounded figure.

So the answer depends on which rate you want: **₹20.43 crore as booked by ITC for FY25**, versus **roughly ₹19.24 crore if you convert the A$2.86m at today's spot rate**. The Australian dollar has strengthened considerably against the rupee since ITC's year-end — the closing rate in the report was 53.81, against roughly 67.3 today — so the closing-rate conversion of the rounded A$ figure is well below what ITC actually reported.

- I could not verify a single authoritative spot rate. Quotes in my search results ranged from about 67.20 (Xe) to 68.18 (exchangerates.org.uk) per A$1; I used 67.2859, the mid-market rate from currencyrate.today for 28 September 2026. A rate of 68.18 would instead give about ₹19.50 crore. Treat the rupee figure as indicative, not transactional.
